terra.problem: Job's earlier cry for pity is outside this passage and needs a reference to Job 19:21.
Zophar says he heard an insulting rebuke, but this passage does not identify it as something Job said.
The line about wanting someone to hush assigns a motive to Zophar that the text does not give.
Zophar says those who saw the man will ask where he is. He does not say they will look for him.
Seeking the favor of the poor does not necessarily mean going to them. The text also does not identify them as the very individuals the man oppressed.
The verse says the sons will seek the favor of the poor, not that they will go to them.
The verse does not say the sons travel toward the poor or rule out their leaving home.
The line alludes to Papa Dorin's time in the dark without identifying the drawer, so a baker unfamiliar with his backstory may not understand it.
An appetite that is never satisfied could still fade. Zophar does not say whether it fades.
Equating never being satisfied with never being full conflicts with Zophar's picture of the man filling his stomach in Job 20:23.
The passage does not say that nobody comes to the man's rescue.
The verse does not say the fire consumes the man before it devours what remains in his tent.
The verse does not say the fire stays at the man's tent or establish where it stops.
Zophar speaks of the wicked man, but the passage does not exclude a king from that description.
